short_summary:

Search does not preserve retrievability of past records by their meaning. search_events (mocka_mcp_server.py:162-181) matches the whole query string as a contiguous substring within a single field (if q in val); no tokenization, no AND-of-terms, no stemming. Multi-term conceptual queries return nothing unless the exact contiguous phrase exists in one field. Records are therefore not inheritable by concept search.

Impact:
A future audit searching by concept can get zero results even though the records exist. Retrievability of a record degrades with how a searcher phrases the query, not with whether the content is present.

Live reproduction (read-only):
- Query "reverse traceability" (contiguous, present verbatim) -> 1 hit (E20260714_716973138f8f4, the W-2 record).
- Query "reverse traceability improvement candidate" (same record, terms scattered) -> 0 hits.
- The W-2 event became unfindable by its own key terms minutes after being written.
- Explains earlier W-1 zero-hit queries (scattered-term queries) vs the "source=chatgpt" hit (contiguous).

Corpus primary data (data/mocka_events.db, 15764 events):
- 187 events mojibake-flagged and unrestorable (title/short_summary permanently corrupted; unfindable by intended words; lost from time-series reconstruction).

Nearly half the corpus is an alternate schema generation where field semantics (who_actor meaning, ID formats, related_event_id overloading observed in W-1) may not carry the same meaning across generations.

1. Missing trace: multi-term concept queries lose all results; cross-record relationships (event/decision/todo/artifact links from W-1/W-2) not traversable via search; mojibake records unrecoverable; top-30 score cap gives no chronological-completeness guarantee.

4. Human Gate required: adopting a new search contract (tokenized AND-search / FTS5 / ranking) = new search convention; any events.db schema or canonical-data mutation; re-interpretation of existing records (e.g. re-indexing mojibake with recovered text); decision on whether old search-result behavior must remain reproducible.
